questionText: The 'Simplicity vs Complexity' (or multiplexity) feature of an attitude system denotes:

options.text: Refers to how many distinct ideas, beliefs, or constituent elements make up the attitude system
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Nature of Attitudes.

options.text: Refers to whether the attitude was taught by a mother or a father
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Refers to the physical grammatical length of the sentence expressing the attitude
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Refers to whether an attitude was learned in kindergarten or in college
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Attitude and Social Cognition (Nature of Attitudes):
Refers to how many distinct ideas, beliefs, or constituent elements make up the attitude system

Detailed Context:
Simplicity-complexity (multiplexity) refers to the number of attitudes or beliefs within a broader attitude system; a simple attitude consists of only one or two beliefs, whereas a complex (multiplex) attitude system contains numerous interconnected beliefs.
Hence Option B is correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

The tendency to attribute our own successes to internal dispositional factors (ability, hard work) and our failures to external situational factors (bad luck, unfair rules)

Hence Option A is correct.
